title: 1992 AHSME Problem 10
statement: The number of positive integers \(k\) for which the equation \[ kx-12=3k \] has an integer solution for \(x\) is

solutions.text:
Solving gives \(x=3+\frac{12}{k}.\) Thus \(x\) is an integer precisely when \(k\) is a positive divisor of \(12.\) The possibilities are \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(6,\) and \(12,\) for a total of \(6.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Solve the equation for \(x\) in terms of \(k\)
The expression \(3+\frac{12}{k}\) is integral exactly when \(k\) is a positive divisor of \(12\)
